raw_graphql_pull_request.body: ### What does this PR do? This PR adds support for FP8 KV cache quantization in vLLM rollout, providing significant memory savings during inference. The KV cache quantization can be used independently or combined with weight and activation FP8 quantization https://github.com/volcengine/verl/blob/main/docs/advance/fp8.md. **How it works:** Leverage vllm to dynamically calculate qkv scales for FP8 KV cache quantization(requires vllm 0.11.2).​ vllm only performs the calculation in the first forward. For RL training, the calculation needs to be triggered every training step to adapt to the new model weights. ​After weights update of each training step, reset the `calculate_kv_scales` flag to True for all the attention layers.​ So for FP8 rollout, functionally we can have: - FP8-linear W8A8 - KV cache FP8 (for storage only) - FP8-linear W8A8 + KV cache FP8 (for storage and attention calculation)​ As this function requires vllm 0.11.2, the PR also includes some changes for v0.11.2 compatibility **Experiments and results:** - Model: Qwen3-8B-Base - Configuration​: - DAPO recipe. AIME24 online validation.​ - 1*8*H100. veRL, FP8 async rollout, vllm+FSDP​ - Prompt batch size 32​ - Rollout batch size: 32x3x16​ - Train_batch_size & ppo_mini_batch_size 32​ - Max response length 20K​ - Token-level TIS, C=2​ - vllm0.11.2+cuda12.9+DeepGEMM+CUDA Graph - Accuracy: - KV cache FP8 aligns well with BF16 on online validation. Full FP8 is also mostly aligned. - Performance: - FP8 linear W8A8 vs BF16: up to 20% speedup​ - KV cache FP8 only vs BF16: ~38% rollout speedup.​ - FP8 linear W8A8 + KV cache FP8 vs BF16 about ~44% speedup ​ ### Checklist Before Starting - [ ] Search for similar PRs. Paste at least one query link here: ... - [ ] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}` (This will be checked by the CI) - `{modules}` include `fsdp`, `megatron`, `sglang`, `vllm`, `rollout`, `trainer`, `ci`, `training_utils`, `recipe`, `hardware`, `deployment`, `ray`, `worker`, `single_controller`, `misc`, `perf`, `model`, `algo`, `env`, `tool`, `ckpt`, `doc`, `data` - If this PR involves multiple modules, separate them with `,` like `[megatron, fsdp, doc]` - `{type}` is in `feat`, `fix`, `refactor`, `chore`, `test` - If this PR breaks any API (CLI arguments, config, function signature, etc.), add `[BREAKING]` to the beginning of the title. - Example: `[BREAKING][fsdp, megatron] feat: dynamic batching` ### Test > For changes that can not be tested by CI (e.g., algorithm implementation, new model support), validate by experiment(s) and show results like training curve plots, evaluation results, etc. ### API and Usage Example > Demonstrate how the API changes if any, and provide usage example(s) if possible. ```python # Add code snippet or script demonstrating how to use this ``` ### Design & Code Changes > Demonstrate the high-level design if this PR is complex, and list the specific changes. ### Checklist Before Submitting > [!IMPORTANT] > Please check all the following items before requesting a review, otherwise the reviewer might deprioritize this PR for review. - [ ] Read the [Contribute Guide](https://github.com/volcengine/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md). - [ ] Apply [pre-commit checks](https://github.com/volcengine/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#code-linting-and-formatting): `pre-commit install && pre-commit run --all-files --show-diff-on-failure --color=always` - [ ] Add / Update [the documentation](https://github.com/volcengine/verl/tree/main/docs). - [ ] Add unit or end-to-end test(s) to [the CI workflow](https://github.com/volcengine/verl/tree/main/.github/workflows) to cover all the code. Hello! I have successfully replicated the KV cache FP8 quantization in sharonyu-115:kv-cache-fp8, which has significantly improve the throughput. But why hasn't this PR been merged until now and suspended for 3 months, is there anything wrong and is there anything I can help?

> Hello! I have successfully replicated the KV cache FP8 quantization in sharonyu-115:kv-cache-fp8, which has significantly improve the throughput. But why hasn't this PR been merged until now and suspended for 3 months, is there anything wrong and is there anything I can help? Hi @LZC-BELIEVER Thanks for the feedback. I was trying to run experiments with MoE models to verify the convergence. On Qwen3-30B DAPO, the observation was on MoE the training had some instability spike, though it was corrected (curves attached as a reference) and on AIME24 it got to 0.5. So I would say the feature is experimental and can be further delved into finer quantization granularity. On the other hand, I will have to rebase the PR code. Would you share a bit about your training scenario and observations?

@sharonyu-115 So excited to see your reply! Firstly, I tried on Qwen3-8B-Base GRPO, using MATH dataset, and I can see that opening FP8 KV cache could show the highest throughput (around 10% promotion) and the lowest gen time. Secondly, I also tried on Qwen2.5-Math-7B GRPO with MATH dateset, and saw a terrible result: The accuracy became around 0 when I open FP8 KV cache, and response was irregular like"????////". I compared the model structure between Qwen2.5 and Qwen3, and found that in qwen3 model there is QK-Norm which could reduce outliers and help stabilize the KV cache quantization. Maybe it is better to add some specific process for models without QK-Norm. Your experiment above is interesting and I have seen similar result in my previous experiment on FlashRL . If it is the problem, I would try to repeat on Qwen3-30B DAPO and see what I can do to help. Did you use the script verl/recipe/dapo/run_dapo_qwen3_moe_30b_vllm_fp8_rollout.sh on the experiment you mentioned?

> Your experiment above is interesting and I have seen similar result in my previous experiment on FlashRL . If it is the problem, I would try to repeat on Qwen3-30B DAPO and see what I can do to help. Did you use the script verl/recipe/dapo/run_dapo_qwen3_moe_30b_vllm_fp8_rollout.sh on the experiment you mentioned?

Hi @LZC-BELIEVER That would be great if you can also run an experiment. Thanks! Yes, you can use that script. While in my run one difference is I used `train_prompt_bsz=128` `train_prompt_mini_bsz=128`,`gen_prompt_bsz=128*3`.

## Code Review

This pull request introduces support for FP8 KV cache quantization in the vLLM rollout, which is a valuable feature for improving memory efficiency and inference performance. The changes are well-structured, including updates to configuration, new utility functions for validation and patching vLLM, and integration into the rollout server and worker logic. The compatibility fixes for different vLLM versions and the critical patches to preserve model parameter attributes during quantization are particularly well-handled. My review identifies one issue regarding a `print` statement that should be replaced with a logger call for better logging practices. Overall, this is a high-quality contribution.

![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

Using `print()` for logging is discouraged in library code as it bypasses the configured logging framework and can lead to unmanageable output in production environments. Please replace this with a `logger.info()` or `logger.debug()` call for consistency with the rest of the codebase.

```suggestion
            logger.info("vllm version is 0.11.1 or higher, calling init_app_state with 3 parameters")
```

+def validate_kv_cache_fp8_config(config):
+    """
+    Validate KV cache FP8 configuration to ensure both kv_cache_dtype=fp8 and

+    Args:
+        config: RolloutConfig with nested quantization config

+    Raises:

+    quant_config = config.quantization
+    kv_cache_dtype = quant_config.kv_cache_dtype
+    calculate_kv_scales = quant_config.calculate_kv_scales
+

+    is_kv_fp8 = kv_cache_dtype is not None and 'fp8' in str(kv_cache_dtype).lower()

+    if calculate_kv_scales and not is_kv_fp8:
+        raise ValueError(
+            "calculate_kv_scales=True requires kv_cache_dtype to be set to fp8. "
+            f"Got calculate_kv_scales={calculate_kv_scales}, kv_cache_dtype={kv_cache_dtype}"
+        )
+    if is_kv_fp8 and not calculate_kv_scales:
+        raise ValueError(
+            "kv_cache_dtype=fp8 requires calculate_kv_scales=True for dynamic scale calculation. "
+            f"Got kv_cache_dtype={kv_cache_dtype}, calculate_kv_scales={calculate_kv_scales}"
+        )
+    
+    logger.debug(f"KV cache FP8 config validated: kv_cache_dtype={kv_cache_dtype}, calculate_kv_scales={calculate_kv_scales}")
+    
+    return kv_cache_dtype, calculate_kv_scales
+
+def is_kv_cache_fp8_enabled(config):

+    logger.debug(f"Checking if FP8 KV cache with dynamic scale calculation is enabled: {config}")

+def reset_kv_scale_flags_in_model(model_runner) -> int:
+    """
+    Reset calculate_kv_scales flags in model_runner and all attention layers.
+    Also restore range constants (q_range, k_range, v_range) that may have been
+    corrupted during wake_up.
+    
+    This should be called after loading new weights to trigger KV scale recalculation
+    on the next forward pass.
+    Args:
+        model_runner: vLLM ModelRunner instance
+        
+    Returns:
+        int: Number of attention layers where flags were reset
+    """
+    logger.info(f"Resetting KV scale calculation flags in model_runner: {model_runner}")
+    
+    # Import vllm envs to get the scale constants
+    from vllm import envs
+    
+    # Reset model_runner level flag
+    if hasattr(model_runner, 'calculate_kv_scales'):
+        model_runner.calculate_kv_scales = True
+        logger.debug("Reset model_runner.calculate_kv_scales = True")
+    else:
+        logger.debug("model_runner does not have calculate_kv_scales attribute")
+    
+    # Reset per-layer flags and restore range constants
+    model = model_runner.model
+    num_reset = 0
+    num_ranges_restored = 0
+    
+    for name, module in model.named_modules():
+        if hasattr(module, 'calculate_kv_scales'):
+            module.calculate_kv_scales = True
+            num_reset += 1
+            
+            # CRITICAL FIX: Restore range constants that get corrupted during wake_up
+            # These are used as denominators in scale calculation: scale = max_value / range
+            # If range becomes 0 or garbage, we get inf/nan
+            ranges_restored = False
+            if hasattr(module, 'q_range') and module.q_range is not None:
+                try:
+                    module.q_range.data.fill_(envs.Q_SCALE_CONSTANT)
+                    ranges_restored = True
+                except Exception as e:
+                    logger.warning(f"Failed to restore q_range for {name}: {e}")
+            
+            if hasattr(module, 'k_range') and module.k_range is not None:
+                try:
+                    module.k_range.data.fill_(envs.K_SCALE_CONSTANT)
+                    ranges_restored = True
+                except Exception as e:
+                    logger.warning(f"Failed to restore k_range for {name}: {e}")
+            
+            if hasattr(module, 'v_range') and module.v_range is not None:
+                try:
+                    module.v_range.data.fill_(envs.V_SCALE_CONSTANT)
+                    ranges_restored = True
+                except Exception as e:
+                    logger.warning(f"Failed to restore v_range for {name}: {e}")
+            
+            if ranges_restored:
+                num_ranges_restored += 1
+    
+    if num_reset > 0:
+        logger.info(f"Reset calculate_kv_scales flag in {num_reset} attention layers")
+        logger.info(f"Restored range constants (q/k/v_range) in {num_ranges_restored} layers (fixes inf/nan)")
+    else:
+        logger.warning("No attention layers with calculate_kv_scales found")
+    
+    return num_reset

reviews.body:
## Code Review

This pull request introduces support for FP8 KV cache quantization in the vLLM rollout, which is a valuable feature for improving memory efficiency and inference performance. The changes are well-structured, including updates to configuration, new utility functions for validation and patching vLLM, and integration into the rollout server and worker logic. The compatibility fixes for different vLLM versions and the critical patches to preserve model parameter attributes during quantization are particularly well-handled. My review identifies one issue regarding a `print` statement that should be replaced with a logger call for better logging practices. Overall, this is a high-quality contribution.
